Blog Review: Sept. 30

Shares

Quantum computing applications; monitoring shared memory; simulating solid state batteries; trusting ML in automotive; integrating standards.

September 30th, 2026 -

By: Jesse Allen

Synopsys’ Prith Banerjee points to graph partitioning for large FEA and CFD simulations as an area where quantum computing already has useful applications within larger workflows.
Cadence’s Divya Bora explains AMBA AXI5 MPAM, which provides a framework for controlling and monitoring shared memory system resources, and the new resource-context correctness challenge it adds to standard AXI protocol verification.
Siemens’ Anna De Gol examines how simulation can support the development of solid-state batteries through a multi-physics, multi-scale modeling workflow that directly links the battery microstructure to its degradation and overall performance.
Keysight’s Sophie Gerken warns that as ML models become increasingly embedded in automotive systems, trust requires confidence that the AI behaves appropriately within its intended context.
Arm’s Joe McIntyre introduces the Arm Architecture Machine Readable Specification, which provides programmatic access to architecture information in a consistent structure that software can use as a foundation for automating architecture-related tasks.
SEMI’s Kartikey Srivastava chats with Daniele Pagano of STMicroelectronics about how integrating standards earlier in the development lifecycle can help bridge the gap between lab innovation and commercial deployment.
Plus, check out the blogs featured in the latest Systems & Design newsletter:
Technology editor Brian Bailey questions whether AI can be creative and asserts that it is impossible to know unless we understand what creativity really means, and that’s difficult to describe.
Arteris’ Ashley Stevens outlines how to transport native packetized NoC traffic directly across die boundaries using a stable, invariant interface.
Siemens EDA’s Keith Felton and Todd Burkholder explain why design data management, traceability, and revision control are critical for multi-chiplet heterogeneous integration.
Keysight EDA’s Fahad Usmani examines the impact of cryogenic temperatures on advanced compact models.
Cadence’s Vinod Khera digs into how agentic systems make choices, how to ensure they are validated, and who’s accountable at final sign-off.
